agent: T-BOOK-037 r0 (u1:c05 authoring, session web-c414c074 chat 08b3170a trace 1a16517d60dbb92d)
what: V4 banned_regex '\\(l\\)' (chem.yaml) fires on the LEGITIMATE liquid state symbol — e.g. H2O(l), Pb(l), 2H2O(l) — which u1:c05 teaches for the first time in the corpus (state symbols are a 1.25 objective of this chapter). The rule was written to catch the OCR artifact class where a capital I is misread as lowercase l (e.g. 'copper(Il)' in chunks 0145/0167/0210), but the plain '(l)' regex cannot distinguish correct state-symbol notation from that artifact. Four sections flagged as errors; all four are correct chemistry.
why: The false positive blocks every state-symbol-bearing section of this and future chapters (c06 part 2 carries the same objective family); an author following the lint literally would strip correct notation.
fix: Rule refined in the same PR: banned_regex '\\(l\\)' -> '\\([Ii]l+\\)' — matches the actual identity-misread class ((Il), (il), (Ill)) while freeing the correct (l) state symbol. The corpus artifacts of record are exactly (Il)/(Ill) forms; no legitimate notation matches the refined pattern.
root_cause: The rule predates the first state-symbol-teaching chapter; the artifact class and the valid notation share the '(l)' surface form only when the I/l distinction is dropped, which the refined pattern captures precisely.
